newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialist privatisation moves to take time.
newsitem.headline: French Socialist privatisation moves to take time.

text.p: Key decisions by France's opposition Socialists concerning privatisation policy could take months after a leftist victory in the French parliamentary election, Socialist former prime minister Michel Rocard said in an interview made public on Monday.

Rocard told the financial daily Les Echos that it would, for example, take the Socialists four months to determine how to handle the planned privatisation of France Telecom, should they win the May 25-June 1 election.
As for state-owned airline Air France, "we have the quasi-obligation, at the European level, to carry out this privatisation. But it's not written in stone.

"It is very important, in managing our territory, to assure the continuity of domestic lines. So I would be in favour of reopening negotiations so that, should the privatisation take place, the state would eventually buy back a company so that this function of managing our territory could be assured," he said.
"We want to be pragmatic, which is often difficult in the midst of an election campaign," Rocard said. "We do not wish to decree a halt to all privatisations."

He said various pending privatisation plans would be weighed according to three functions he said the state must fulfill: providing all citizens with equal access to services, managing the territory, and assuring strategic interests such as self-sufficiency in energy and food.
